newsitem.title: INDIA: India says not to hike oil prices in short term.
newsitem.headline: India says not to hike oil prices in short term.

text.p: India on Friday ruled out plans to hike oil prices in the short term.
"There will be no price hike in the immediate future," T.R. Baalu, minister of state for petroleum and natural gas told a news conference.

Analysts say an oil price hike is unavoidable if the government is to reduce the oil pool deficit, a subsidy it pays oil companies to compensate them for selling oil in the domestic market at prices below international levels.
"We have ways and means of tackling the situation," Baalu said, but refused to elaborate. "If the situation gets out of control, we will see."
Baalu said the oil pool deficit was 158 billion rupees ($4.4 billion) and total subsidies on petroleum products amounted to 184.4 billion.
State-run Indian Oil Corporation (IOC) would launch an issue of global depositary receipts in the financial year 1997/98 (April-March), Baalu said.
"We are waiting for a congenial atmosphere so the the issue can be fully subscribed and we can get a good price," he said.
The government hoped to raise 20 billion rupees through the sale by divesting 5.0 percent of its stake, he added.
Baalu said the government wanted to develop minor ports so as to reduce infrastructure bottlenecks in the import of oil and oil products.
A decision would be taken within two months on the recommendations of an expert committee set up to examine ways to deregulate the state-controlled oil sector, he said.
